task: Build a new freelance finance tracking phone app: an Expo (React Native) app for iOS and Android that uses the phone's camera to photograph receipts (with a photo-library fallback), plus a Python FastAPI backend (PostgreSQL in production; SQLite via DATABASE_URL for tests and previews). Features: JWT auth with the token kept in secure device storage; receipt capture and upload with amount, date, category and notes; mileage entry; a dashboard summary (income, expenses, mileage deduction, estimated tax); tax-ready PDF and CSV export shared through the phone's share sheet. The UI must be polished and professional, with a best‑practice sign‑up and sign‑in flow and clear navigation to every action. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests.
validation: python syntax ok, ruff ok, python dependencies install ok, npm install (expo-app) ok, expo dependency versions (expo-app) ok, expo export (expo-app) ok, expo web export (expo-app) ok, ui backend starts (expo-app) ok, ui renders (expo-app) ok, ui styles applied (expo-app) ok, accessibility, serious or critical (expo-app) FAIL, responsive layout on a phone (expo-app) ok, ui primary flow (expo-app) ok, typescript (tsc) ok, json syntax ok, scanner suppressions ok, semgrep (security errors) ok, trivy secrets ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (high/critical, fixable) ok, trivy misconfigurations (high/critical) ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (other) warn, planned files present ok

issues: Accessibility – role-img-alt violations: Screens (empty dashboard, receipt capture, and possibly other screens) render images with role="img" but without an accessible name (no alt text, aria‑label, aria‑labelledby, or title). This triggers a serious accessibility error and blocks the static validation. Add appropriate accessibilityLabel (or aria‑label/etc.) to every Image component used in the UI, especially placeholder/illustration images on the Dashboard and ReceiptCapture screens, so that screen readers can convey meaningful information.
review.feedback: All acceptance tests pass, but the static validation fails due to serious accessibility issues. Ensure every image rendered in the Expo app includes an accessible label (e.g., <Image source={...} accessibilityLabel="..." />) or appropriate ARIA attributes. After fixing the missing alt text, re-run the validation.

stalled: phase 1 (function) did not finish in 12 rounds

security.summary: Skipped until tests and validation pass.

deployment_guide.app_type: mobile app (Expo / React Native), web service or API

ui.summary: The app loads, passes axe and Lighthouse, and the primary flow works, but several design‑system and accessibility gaps remain that break the spec or degrade the user experience. These gaps include missing interaction states (focus outlines, hover/pressed colors), incomplete sign‑up/in forms (no password show/hide toggle, no live rule list, missing autocomplete attributes, submit button can be silently disabled), missing empty‑state copy in the Dashboard, missing error‑toast copy for some API failures, missing persistent navigation on the web drawer, and some design‑token misuse (hard‑coded colors/sizes in a few components). Because these issues prevent the product from meeting the spec’s “no forward path missing” and accessibility requirements, they are flagged as high severity.

findings.issue: Sign‑up form lacks a password visibility toggle, live validation rule list, and autocomplete attributes; also the submit button becomes disabled without a visible loading indicator, violating sign‑up best practices and the specified copy.
findings.fix: Add a show/hide eye icon button with proper `accessibilityLabel` and `accessibilityState` to toggle `secureTextEntry`. Render the live rule list under the password field and link it to the input via `aria‑describedby`. Set `autoComplete="email"` and `autoComplete="new-password"`. Ensure the "Create account" button shows a loading spinner with the text "Creating account…" and is not silently disabled.

findings.issue: Sign‑in form also misses the password show/hide toggle, autocomplete attributes, and focus‑visible outlines; the loading state does not display the exact "Signing you in…" message.
findings.fix: Implement the same password visibility toggle as sign‑up, add `autoComplete="email"` and `autoComplete="current-password"`, render a loading overlay with the spinner and the text "Signing you in…", and ensure all focusable elements have a 2 px solid `primary` outline on focus.

findings.issue: Empty state on the Dashboard uses placeholder text instead of the exact copy "You haven’t added any receipts or mileage yet. Tap the + button to get started." and the CTA button label does not match "Add first receipt". Also the offline banner copy is missing.
findings.fix: Update the EmptyState component to display the exact title "No data yet", body copy as specified, and a PrimaryButton labelled "Add first receipt". Add a Banner component that shows "You’re offline – data may be outdated." when the app detects offline status, using the correct token colors.

findings.issue: Button styling uses hard‑coded hex colors and dimensions instead of the `theme.colors.primary` and `theme.spacing` tokens, breaking the design‑token contract.
findings.fix: Replace all inline color values with `theme.colors.primary`/`theme.colors.primaryVariant` etc., and use `theme.spacing.lg` for padding, `theme.roundness` for border radius. Ensure the `minHeight` is 48 px and `minWidth` is 120 px as defined.

findings.issue: Cards use a hard‑coded shadow style instead of the `elevation.card` token and have a static width that can cause horizontal scrolling on narrow phones (<390 px).
findings.fix: Apply `...theme.elevation.card` for elevation, set `maxWidth: 360` and `marginHorizontal: theme.spacing.lg` to respect global max‑content width, and verify no overflow occurs.

findings.issue: Root `<View>` does not have `accessibilityRole="main"` and lacks proper safe‑area handling; on devices with notches the bottom tab bar can be overlapped.
findings.fix: Wrap the content in a `<SafeAreaView accessibilityRole="main">` and apply `paddingBottom: theme.spacing.lg` to avoid overlap with the FAB and tab bar.

findings.issue: Permission prompt modal does not include the exact copy "FinanceMate needs camera access to photograph receipts." and the fallback “Choose from library” button label differs. Also missing error toast copy for upload failures.
findings.fix: Update the permission modal text to match the spec, ensure the fallback button is labeled exactly "Choose from library", and standardize toast messages to use "Upload failed. Check your connection and try again." as defined.

findings.issue: Missing loading overlay with the exact "Saving mileage…" message and missing error toast copy "Failed to save mileage. Please try again.". Also the Save button can be disabled without a visible spinner.
findings.fix: Render a full‑screen overlay with a spinner and the text "Saving mileage…" during the API call. Show the error toast with the exact copy on failure. Keep the Save button enabled with a loading state indicator.

findings.issue: Export buttons lack disabled state styling and do not show a spinner next to the CSV/PDF button with the exact "Generating CSV…" / "Generating PDF…" messages. Toast after share does not use the specified copy.
findings.fix: When export starts, disable both buttons, show a spinner next to the active button, and display a temporary banner with the required message. After sharing, show a toast "Report ready to share."

findings.issue: On web, the left drawer navigation is hidden and the bottom tab bar remains visible, violating the spec that the drawer should provide navigation and the bottom tab bar should be hidden on desktop.
findings.fix: Add a breakpoint that hides `<BottomNavigation>` when viewport width >= 1280 px and renders `<Drawer>` with the same navigation items. Ensure the drawer respects the 240 px width and uses the `surface` token for background.

findings.issue: The EmptyState component does not include a visible focus outline for the CTA button when navigated via keyboard, nor does it expose a proper `role="alertdialog"` for screen readers.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityRole="alertdialog"` to the container and ensure the CTA button receives the standard focus outline (2 px solid `primary`).

findings.issue: Form fields lack the required `nativeID` + `accessibilityLabel` linking, and the error `HelperText` is not associated via `accessibilityDescribedBy`, breaking the accessible error indication pattern.
findings.fix: Generate a unique `nativeID` for each TextInput, set the corresponding label’s `htmlFor` (or `accessibilityLabel`), and pass the error ID to `HelperText` via `accessibilityDescribedBy`.

findings.issue: Tab items do not expose `role="tab"` and `aria‑selected` (or `accessibilityState={{ selected }}`) attributes, and the focus ring on tabs is missing, violating keyboard navigation and visible focus requirements.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityRole="tab"` and `accessibilityState={{ selected }}` to each tab button, and apply a 2 px solid `primary` outline when focused.

findings.issue: Toast component does not call `announceForAccessibility` on mount, so screen readers do not announce success or error messages, contrary to the accessibility spec.
findings.fix: Import `announceForAccessibility` from `react-native` and invoke it with the toast message when the component mounts.

findings.issue: Some screens contain unused CSS class names (e.g., `container`, `wrapper`) without corresponding style rules, indicating styling is not applied as intended.
findings.fix: Remove unused class names or create matching style definitions using the Design Tokens. Verify with the style audit that `unmatchedCount` remains 0.

findings.issue: Media endpoint does not enforce rate‑limiting on per‑user basis and returns raw files without `Cache‑Control` headers, risking DoS and leaking data. While not a UI issue, it violates the spec’s security expectations for forward navigation and data protection.
findings.fix: Add a per‑user rate limit (e.g., `@limiter.limit("5/minute")`) and set appropriate `Cache-Control: private, max‑age=0` headers on `FileResponse`.

findings.issue: No visible type scale or consistent typography hierarchy (e.g., heading, body, link).
findings.fix: Apply a proper type scale: use a larger, bolder font for the heading, medium for labels, and small for the link text. Ensure consistent spacing between text elements.

findings.issue: Fields and button are aligned left, but there’s no visible grid or spacing system. Padding and margins are inconsistent, making it feel unstyled.
findings.fix: Implement a consistent grid system with equal spacing around fields and the button. Use padding and margin utilities to create rhythm and alignment.

findings.issue: The 'Log in' button is centered horizontally, but the link text is not aligned to the same vertical baseline, creating visual imbalance.
findings.fix: Align the link text vertically with the button’s center or baseline for visual harmony. Consider using a consistent spacing above and below the button and link.

findings.issue: The emoji next to the button is unstyled and out of place. It doesn’t contribute to the user experience and feels like a placeholder.
findings.fix: Remove the emoji or replace it with a branded icon or subtle decorative element that aligns with the app’s identity.

findings.issue: No indication of form field validation or error states. The screen assumes users will enter correct data.
findings.fix: Add inline error messages under fields when validation fails. Use consistent error styling (e.g., red text, icon) to guide users.

findings.issue: visual quality 6/10 on 'sign in' (needs 8+): The sign-in screen is functional but lacks polish. It's clean and readable, with clear visual hierarchy and a primary action, but it uses browser-default styling, has no type scale or grid alignment, and the layout feels unstyled and minimal. It's acceptable for a basic MVP but not polished enough for a premium product.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Password field lacks a visible password visibility toggle icon; the hint text is placed below the field but not visually linked to it, reducing usability.
findings.fix: Add a password visibility toggle icon (eye icon) to the right of the password field. Visually anchor the hint text to the password field using consistent spacing and alignment.

findings.issue: The 'Already have an account? Log in' link is centered horizontally but not vertically aligned with the main form, creating an asymmetrical layout.
findings.fix: Vertically center the link within its container to align with the form’s vertical rhythm.

findings.issue: The 'Create account' button is slightly too wide for the screen, causing it to appear cramped in the center.
findings.fix: Adjust button width to fit comfortably within the container, or reduce padding to improve fit without sacrificing readability.

findings.issue: The desktop layout is not visible; only the phone version is provided. This prevents assessment of desktop-specific issues like spacing, grid alignment, or form scaling.
findings.fix: Provide a desktop screenshot to evaluate layout, spacing, and form sizing for larger screens.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'sign up' (needs 8+): The sign-up screen is clean and functional, with clear visual hierarchy and a strong primary action. Typography is readable, spacing is generous, and alignment is consistent. However, it lacks polish in form design and desktop adaptation, and the password hint is visually disconnected from the field.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The empty state message lacks visual hierarchy; 'No data yet' is the same weight as the supporting text, making the primary action less prominent.
findings.fix: Make 'No data yet' bold or larger, and use a lighter weight or smaller size for the supporting text to create visual hierarchy.

findings.issue: The orange '+' button is visually secondary to the blue 'Add first receipt' button, but they are not aligned or grouped consistently — the button is floating to the right, which breaks visual alignment.
findings.fix: Align the orange '+' button with the blue button, either by placing it inside the button or positioning it directly to the right with consistent spacing.

findings.issue: The primary CTA 'Add first receipt' button is not touch-friendly; its width is too narrow for a finger tap, and it’s not visually distinct enough from the surrounding space.
findings.fix: Increase the button width to at least 80% of the screen width, or add a larger hit area with padding. Use a more pronounced shadow or border to make it stand out.

findings.issue: The desktop layout stretches the content too wide, making the empty state appear sparse and underutilized. The content is centered but not anchored to a grid, leaving large empty spaces on the sides.
findings.fix: Use a consistent grid to align the empty state content. Consider left-aligning the text and buttons, or using a centered column with padding to create a more balanced layout.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'empty dashboard' (needs 8+): The dashboard empty state is clean and functional, with a clear primary action and consistent navigation. However, it lacks visual polish and hierarchy that would elevate it to a polished, premium product.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Desktop layout is stretched and lacks proper spacing. The content is centered with no left/right padding, making it feel cramped and unprofessional. The FAB is positioned awkwardly near the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Apply a consistent grid system with padding on desktop. Center the content vertically and horizontally, and reposition the FAB to align with the bottom navigation bar or place it in a more natural location (e.g., top-right corner).

findings.issue: The FAB (orange + button) is partially cut off on the desktop view, obscuring part of the text 'Offi...ies' below it.
findings.fix: Adjust the FAB’s position or size to ensure full visibility on desktop. Consider using a fixed position or adjusting the layout to accommodate the FAB without clipping.

findings.issue: The bottom navigation bar icons are not fully aligned with the text labels (e.g., 'Dashboard' is slightly offset).
findings.fix: Align the icons and text labels to the same baseline for consistency and professionalism.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'dashboard with receipt' (needs 8+): The dashboard is clean and functional with clear visual hierarchy and a prominent primary action (FAB). Typography is readable with consistent scale. Spacing and alignment are generally good on both views. However, the desktop version lacks proper layout and spacing, and the FAB placement on desktop is awkward. The app is polished enough for a commercial product but lacks the refinement of top-tier apps.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Form fields are cramped with insufficient vertical spacing between them and the 'Save mileage' button, making the form feel dense and hard to scan.
findings.fix: Increase vertical spacing between form fields and the button to create breathing room and improve scannability.

findings.issue: The 'Mileage entries' section below the form is empty and lacks any visual guidance or placeholder to indicate the user should scroll or tap to add entries.
findings.fix: Add a subtle placeholder text or icon (e.g., 'No entries yet. Add your first mileage entry.') to guide the user.

findings.issue: The form fields have no labels above them, which violates the spec's requirement for labels above fields and makes the form less accessible and harder to understand.
findings.fix: Add clear, top-aligned labels above each input field (e.g., 'Date', 'Miles driven') to improve usability and accessibility.

findings.issue: The 'Notes (optional)' field is visually identical to the other fields, but its label doesn't match the spec's 'optional' hint, and the field size is not optimized for touch.
findings.fix: Add a small '(optional)' hint inline with the field (e.g., 'Notes (optional)' or 'Notes (optional) — tap to add') and ensure the field is touch-friendly (minimum 44px height).

findings.issue: The layout is stretched and unstyled, with elements aligned to the left edge and no responsive design. It looks like a browser fallback, not a polished desktop app.
findings.fix: Redesign the desktop layout to use a proper grid system, center the content, and adjust spacing to utilize the full width without stretching. Add padding and visual hierarchy.

findings.issue: The 'Save mileage' button is blue, but the app's brand color is not consistently applied elsewhere (e.g., navigation icons, header).
findings.fix: Apply the brand color consistently to all primary actions and navigation elements to reinforce brand identity.

findings.issue: visual quality 6/10 on 'mileage entry' (needs 8+): The screen is functional and follows basic design principles, but lacks polish and visual hierarchy. The form is cramped, spacing is inconsistent, and there's no visual guidance for the empty state. On desktop, it's stretched and unstyled, making it feel like a browser fallback. The primary action is clear, but the overall experience feels raw and unrefined.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The form fields are visually identical to browser default inputs with no custom styling (border radius, padding, placeholder text, or focus states).
findings.fix: Apply consistent, branded styling to inputs: rounded corners, subtle inner shadow, placeholder text, and visual feedback on focus.

findings.issue: The 'Save mileage' button is a solid blue rectangle with no visual hierarchy or depth cues (elevation, shadow, or gradient) to make it feel like a premium action.
findings.fix: Add subtle elevation or shadow to the button. Consider a gradient or glossy finish for premium feel. Ensure it's visually distinct from the form fields.

findings.issue: The 'Save mileage' button is touch-friendly (width > 44px), but the form fields are not clearly separated from the button or the list below, creating visual clutter.
findings.fix: Add subtle padding or spacing around the button and between the form and the list to improve visual breathing room.

findings.issue: The desktop layout is appropriately scaled but feels minimalistic and lacks visual hierarchy. The form fields and list are presented with no visual distinction from the background, making them feel flat and unpolished.
findings.fix: Add subtle background shading or borders to the form container and list section to create depth and separate them from the background.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'mileage list' (needs 8+): Polished, clean interface with clear visual hierarchy and consistent spacing. The primary action is prominent and the form is well-organized. However, it lacks visual polish and brand personality that would elevate it to 8 or 9. The desktop layout is appropriately scaled but feels minimalistic. Touch targets are adequate but could be more inviting.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Buttons are identical in size and color, lacking subtle visual differentiation (e.g., one could be slightly larger or have a different shade to indicate primary action).
findings.fix: Make one button (e.g., Export CSV) slightly larger or use a slightly different shade of blue to subtly indicate it as the primary action, aligning with common conventions.

findings.issue: The header text 'Export your data' is centered, which is acceptable, but could be left-aligned for better alignment with the buttons below and a more modern, grid-aligned feel.
findings.fix: Left-align the header text to align with the left edge of the buttons and improve visual consistency with the grid.

findings.issue: Buttons are identical in size and shape, lacking visual hierarchy to distinguish primary action from secondary (though both are primary actions).
findings.fix: Use subtle visual differentiation: e.g., slightly larger button for CSV, or a different border radius or shadow. Alternatively, add icons to the buttons for visual distinction.

findings.issue: The text 'Export your data' is centered but not visually weighted as a header, lacking a clear type scale.
findings.fix: Increase the font size and weight of the heading to establish a clear visual hierarchy. Use a bold or semi-bold weight for the heading to make it stand out.

findings.issue: The spacing between the buttons is consistent, but the vertical padding around the buttons is minimal, making them feel cramped.
findings.fix: Increase the vertical padding around the buttons to create more breathing room and improve tap targets.

observations: validator 'accessibility, serious or critical (expo-app)' blocked 9 of 12 rounds
coder hit its turn limit in 6 of 12 rounds ([1, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12])
slowest round 2 took 54 min; average 37 min
went_well: Backend unit test failure (dashboard income) was fixed by round 2, allowing the test suite to pass for the remainder of the run.
The TypeScript compiler errors were eventually reduced to only a few remaining issues, showing the validator‑feedback loop is at least capable of converging on compile‑ready code.
The designer supplied a complete UI flow description (ui_flow.json) that the UI‑flow validator could execute, even though the link click failed.

improvements.title: Give the coder precise, line‑level accessibility fixes
improvements.evidence: Validator "accessibility, serious or critical (expo-app)" blocked 9/12 rounds (rounds 1,2,4,5,6,7,8,10,12).  Errors were broad, e.g., "color‑contrast: Elements must meet minimum ratio…", "role‑img‑alt: Image elements must have alternative text" without file/line hints, causing the coder to guess and miss many instances.
improvements.change: Modify ui_check.mjs (accessibility validator) to report each issue with file path, line number, and a concrete fix suggestion (e.g., add `accessibilityLabel="Receipt preview"` or replace `#0066ff` with a contrast‑approved color).  Also adjust the feedback message to the coder to embed these actionable snippets directly.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder can apply the exact fix in one edit, reducing repeated accessibility failures and eliminating the need for multiple turn‑limit hits.  Faster convergence and fewer rounds spent on the same problem.

improvements.title: Make the design‑system requirement explicit in DESIGN.md and the designer prompt
improvements.evidence: Validator "design system in use" blocked rounds 1 and 2, repeatedly calling out raw React Native components (e.g., "expo-app/src/screens/MileageEntryScreen.tsx: raw React Native TextInput").  The coder kept using raw components despite the feedback.
improvements.change: Update the designer prompt to require a component‑mapping table in DESIGN.md for every screen (e.g., `Screen → PaperScreen`, `TextInput → PaperTextInput`, `Button → PaperButton`).  Include sample code snippets.  Extend the design‑system validator to check for those exact imports and flag each missing mapping with file/line location.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives a clear spec of which Paper components replace each raw widget, can replace them in bulk, and the validator will confirm compliance, removing the design‑system blocker early in the pipeline.

improvements.title: Switch the coder to an incremental diff‑only workflow and expose exact dependency versions
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in 6 of 12 rounds (1,5,6,9,10,12) and consumed 17 716 210 prompt tokens, causing the slowest round (2) to take 54 min.  The coder was fed the whole repository each turn, making it hard to stay within the 20‑60 turn budget.
improvements.change: Rewrite the coder prompt to request only the files that changed since the previous round (use a git‑style diff).  Limit edits to ≤5 files per round and include a generated snippet showing the current versions of Expo SDK, react‑native‑paper, and other key packages (pulled via `npm view`).  Provide a small “dependency‑info” block in the prompt.
improvements.expected_effect: Token usage will drop dramatically, turn limits will no longer be hit, and each round will finish faster (average < 20 min).  The coder will also be aware of the exact library versions, reducing TypeScript import errors.

improvements.title: Enforce security scanning every round and auto‑fix vulnerable transitive deps
improvements.evidence: Rounds 5 and 11 reported high‑severity vulnerable packages (braces@3.0.3, node‑forge@1.4.0) and an npm‑install error (sprintf‑js@2.0.0 not found), yet the "security" column shows "skipped" for all rounds, so fixes never happened.
improvements.change: Activate the security scanner (trivy/semgrep) each round and treat any findings as a hard blocker.  Add a new validator that parses `package-lock.json`, removes or upgrades vulnerable packages, and runs `expo install` to regenerate a clean lockfile before compilation.
improvements.expected_effect: Security‑related failures will surface early, the npm‑install validator will succeed, and the pipeline will no longer waste rounds on dependency errors.

improvements.title: Upgrade UI‑flow validator to normalise Unicode and require stable test IDs
improvements.evidence: UI primary flow validator failed in rounds 3 and 9 because the "Don’t have an account? Sign up" link timed out.  In round 9 the reviewer also flagged "no literal escapes in UI text" (e.g., `\u2019` appearing literally).  The link therefore never matched the expected label.
improvements.change: Enhance the ui_flow.json validator to (a) normalise rendered text (convert escaped sequences to actual characters) before matching, and (b) require a dedicated `testID="signup-link"` (or similar) on navigation elements.  Update the reviewer prompt to remind the coder to use `Pressable`/`Button` with that `testID` and a plain‑text `accessibilityLabel`.
improvements.expected_effect: The sign‑up link will be reliably found, eliminating the repeated timeout failures, and the pipeline will progress past the UI‑flow stage without extra rounds.
